## Critique
- claim-1: The strategy establishes the stated conditional certificate. It explicitly classifies every interval Schur basis for \(b<k\le i+j\), handles the terminal class at \(k=i+j+1\), and proves vanishing thereafter. Formula (1), together with \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\), gives the complete multiplication lattice. The displayed \(h_1\)-row matrices have determinant \(1\), proving \((A_+M)_{d+k}=M_{d+k}\) for every remaining nonterminal degree; equation (5) proves the terminal case. Boundary cases, including one-dimensional matrices, are covered. The conclusion remains correctly conditional on the stipulated all-degree interval/Schur/Pieri presentation and makes no parent-theorem claim.
